_note: Hand-authored vectors for linkedCounterWindowHeal.ts ↔ Helpers/LinkedCounterWindowHeal.swift (owner rule 2026-10-01: a counting square on a board accounts only for the counter's logs inside that board's window). Every expectation was hand-computed; the copy ids are literal uuidv5 outputs (name "sources:derived:<boardId>:<root>", computed ONCE with the TS uuidv5) that Swift must reproduce independently. `planLinkedCounterWindowHeal` vectors share the `boards` roster below unless a vector carries its own `boards`. Task rows carry every field the planner reads; `null` = absent. Stamping is all-or-nothing (PR #537 review): an unstamped row is stamped only when every further placing board is a direct placement (and the row has a goal when there is more than one board); a window-stamped row placed on a board it is not stamped for gets a copy for that board.

sameWindowStart.name: fractional vs whole seconds, same instant
offset form vs UTC form, same instant
both unparseable and equal → literal match

isWindowStampedForBoard.name: window-stamped, same instant in the other encoding
no sharedCounterId (a plain wizard-born timeboxed task)

vectors.name: single direct placement → stamp in place, no copy
vectors.note: One live placement: the row takes that board's window.

vectors.name: two direct placements → the EARLIEST board (by startDate) stamps, the later one gets a copy; placement listing order is irrelevant
vectors.note: boardTasks list March first; February still wins the stamp.

vectors.name: direct + reached via a compound → the reached (earlier) board stamps, the later direct placement is copied
vectors.note: compA on February holds hub1 as a child; hub1 is placed directly on March. The FIRST board may be reached (the stamped row is what the compound reads); only FURTHER boards must be direct.

vectors.name: a further board reached only through a compound → NOTHING (the row stays unstamped, no copies)
vectors.note: hub1 direct on January; compA places it on February and March only through the compound. A child link cannot be repointed per board, and a stamped row would read January's window on every board — so no stamp either: the kernel's context-window fallback renders all three boards correctly as long as the row stays unstamped.

vectors.name: reached-only single board → stamp (direct or reached alike)
vectors.note: No direct placement at all; the first (only) board is reached through compA.

vectors.name: unplaced candidate → nothing
vectors.note: A library-only hub-linked row keeps its lifetime display.

vectors.name: window-stamped for February placed on February AND March → one copy for March only, no stamp
vectors.note: A stamped row is never re-stamped; the February placement is its own (isWindowStampedForBoard) and stays; the March placement is mis-placed and gets March's deterministic row.

vectors.name: deleted board and tombstoned placement are ignored
vectors.note: Live placement on a deleted board (b-del) and a tombstoned placement on March both drop out; April is the only live one.

vectors.name: endDate-null (indefinite) board → the stamp carries endDate null
an open-ended board orders by its startDate among the others; copies sort by boardId
vectors.note: Feb 1 (b-feb) < Feb 15 (b-open) < Mar 1 (b-mar): February stamps; copies for b-mar and b-open, listed by boardId.

vectors.name: goal-less linked row on two boards → NOTHING (no target to copy, so no stamp either)
vectors.note: No maxCount means no per-window target for a March copy; stamping February alone would freeze March out once February ends, so the row stays unstamped.

vectors.name: direct and reached on the SAME board count once
vectors.note: compA (holding hub1) and hub1 itself are both on February: one board, one stamp, no copy.

vectors.name: tombstoned link, deleted compound parent and a non-counting linked row are all ignored
vectors.note: compA→hub1 link is tombstoned (February not reached); compDel is deleted (March not reached); normalLinked has a sharedCounterId but is NORMAL (not a candidate).

vectors.name: two candidates → stamps and copies sorted by taskId then boardId
vectors.note: hub2 is listed before hub1 in tasks; output is still hub1 first.

vectors.name: idempotent: the healed state of the two-placement case plans nothing
vectors.note: hub1 stamped for February (createdInWizard set by the stamp) and the March placement repointed at the minted copy row: both rows are window-stamped, nothing is a candidate.

vectors.name: two live placements of one task on one board (malformed) → the smallest boardTask id is repointed
vectors.note: Defensive determinism: bt-y < bt-z.

vectors.name: unparseable startDates fall back to string order
vectors.note: Neither board start parses; "aaa" < "zzz" as strings, so b-bad-z stamps.

vectors.name: goal-less linked row on a single board → stamp
vectors.note: With one placing board there is nothing to copy, so the missing goal does not block the stamp.

vectors.name: direct on the first and third boards, reached only on the second → NOTHING (all-or-nothing)
vectors.note: hub1 direct on January and March; compA places it on February. One further board that cannot be repointed vetoes the whole plan for the row — March is not copied either.

vectors.name: window-stamped for February placed on March only → one copy for March, no stamp
vectors.note: A row stamped for board X placed on board Y (an old-app device placing it, or a wrong "first board" from a partial graph): Y gets derivedTaskId(Y, root); the row keeps its own window.

vectors.name: window-stamped for February placed on February only → nothing
vectors.note: Its own board: isWindowStampedForBoard holds, nothing to plan.

vectors.name: window-stamped for February in the other startDate encoding, placed on February → nothing
vectors.note: The stamp compares instants (sameWindowStart), so a sync re-encoding of startDate is not a mis-placement.

vectors.name: goal-less window-stamped row placed on another board → nothing
vectors.note: No maxCount means no target to copy; the row is left as it is (the kernel reads its stamped window).

vectors.name: a board's own deterministic row stamped for another window → nothing (the Board Edit date path owns its dates)
vectors.note: The task id IS derivedTaskId(b-mar, root-1) but its stamp says February: a copy would repoint the placement at itself every run, so the planner leaves it alone.

vectors.name: idempotent: the mis-placed case after its repoint plans nothing
vectors.note: The March placement now points at the minted March row (stamped for March); the February row is unplaced.

windowStampedCopyDraft.name: full source → draft carries the source's own target/title/action/unit and the copy's window
action-less source keeps its own title; action/unit become empty strings
negative baseline clamps to 0 (source title is the auto one, so it is regenerated unchanged)
custom title kept verbatim: 'Morning pages' != auto 'Read 4 pages' (owner bug 2026-10-06)
auto title regenerated: an end-padded '  Read 4 pages  ' is the auto title after trimming, so the copy gets the clean regenerated 'Read 4 pages'
case-sensitive: 'read 4 pages' differs from auto 'Read 4 pages' only by case and is therefore a CUSTOM title, kept verbatim
empty title is auto: regenerated from the source's fields
continuous source keeps its fractional goal and baseline
discrete source floors a fractional goal and baseline (legacy)
continuous source with a sub-1 goal still gets a copy (R15)
discrete source with a sub-1 goal (malformed) is refused
